chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from one or more, all from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrificial animal (hady), 'What can the one who offers it eat from it during his Tamattu' and other than that?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Just as he eats from his sacrificial animal (for Hajj).'

key_terms.أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ: Aban ibn Uthman, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith collections
key_terms.مُتْعَتِهِ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for eating meat from the sacrificial animal in Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the pilgrim performing Tamattu' may consume meat from the hady in the same manner as one offering the Hajj-specific sacrifice, establishing legal parity between the two. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the distribution and consumption of sacrificial meat, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations found in some Sunni schools. The hadith is situated within the broader context of Hajj rituals, specifically addressing the practicalities of meat distribution after the sacrifice in Mina.
